question.problem:
Previous studies show that the scores of girls and boys on a particular test for dyslexia have standard deviations of $2$ points and $4$ points, respectively. Scientists want to determine whether the population mean ${\mu }_{x}$ for girls is the same as the population mean ${\mu }_{y}$ for boys. They construct a $99%$ confidence interval for the difference between the population means.

Scientists sampled $125$ girls and $118$ boys and found that their mean scores on the test were $42$ points and $41$ points. Which of the following statements are true?

I. The end-points of the $99%$ confidence interval for the difference between the population means are approximately $1\pm 1.055.$

II. All values contained within the $99%$ confidence interval are positive.

III. The confidence interval data suggests that ${\mu }_{x}>{\mu }_{y}.$

*Hint: Given a random variable $Z∼N(0,1),$ the table below shows the $z$-scores ${z}_{p}$ such that $P(Z>{z}_{p})=p$ for some particular values of $p.$*

| $p$ | $0.100$ | $0.050$ | $0.025$ | $0.010$ | $0.005$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ${z}_{p}$ | $1.282$ | $1.645$ | $1.960$ | $2.326$ | $2.576$ |
